item.title: Falcons rule DE Samson Ebukam, WR Zachariah Branch out for Week 9
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Falcons have ruled out a pair of players for this week's game against the Bengals in Madrid.
item.content:encoded:
The Falcons have ruled out a pair of players for this week's game against the Bengals in Madrid.

Head coach Kevin Stefanski said that defensive end Samson Ebukam and wide receiver Zachariah Branch will both miss the game due to hamstring injuries. Stefanski said he does not know if the two players will miss more time.

Ebukam has 11 tackles and 2.5 sacks in seven appearances this season. Branch has 10 catches for 64 yards on offense and he has also served as a punt and kickoff returner.

The Falcons will update the rest of their injuries when they release their first practice report of the week on Wednesday.

item.title: As Giants pursue Jonathan Taylor, could they pivot to Derrick Henry?
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Quarterback injuries could prompt Baltimore to listen to offers for Henry.
item.content:encoded:
The Giants (and other teams) hope to land Colts running back Jonathan Taylor via trade. With Baltimore's season potentially falling apart following Sunday injuries to starting quarterback Lamar Jackson (thumb) and his backup Tyler Huntley (toe), there could be another running back to potentially be pursued at or before the November 10 deadline, by the Giants or other teams.

Derrick Henry, now 32, is far closer to the end of his career than the beginning. His contract pays out $12 million in 2027, with none of it guaranteed.

Now could be the time for the Ravens to turn the remainder of his contract into a draft pick or two.

And the Giants would make plenty of sense. Beyond the fact that the Giants view Taylor as on the second tier of current NFL tailbacks with Henry, Giants coach John Harbaugh has experience with Henry.

After a Week 5 loss to the Saints, Harbaugh explained the distribution of carries to a wide swath of tailbacks by pointing out that they don't have a clear-cut workhorse.

“I would love for us to be in that kind of a circumstance,” Harbaugh said at the time. “A Derrick Henry circumstance or a Saquon Barkley circumstance or whatever it might be."

The best way to be in a "Derrick Henry circumstance" would be to, you know, get Derrick Henry.

Whether the Ravens would trade Henry depends on whether they plan to keep him beyond this season. If they'd cut him before a $1 million roster bonus comes due in March, they wouldn't get a compensatory draft pick. The only way to get value for his contract would be to trade it.

Through eight games, Henry leads the league with 158 carries. He has 632 yards (4.0 per carry) and eight touchdowns.

Given the quarterback injuries in Baltimore, the Ravens surely will get a call or two about Henry. The Giants, given their interest in Taylor, could be one of them.

item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Chiefs rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane has been battling through a shoulder injury throughout the season.
item.content:encoded:
Chiefs rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane has been battling through a shoulder injury throughout the season.

It kept him out of Sunday’s loss to the Broncos, with Delane being downgraded from questionable to out on Saturday.

At this point, it’s unclear if Delane will be able to return for Kansas City’s Week 9 matchup against the Jets.

“It’s just a matter of it being strong enough to get out there,” head coach Andy Reid said in his Monday news conference, via Nate Taylor of ESPN. “There’s a chance that he’ll be able to get himself out there this week. Again, it’s just how strong it is. It’s going to be a day-to-day thing.”

The No. 6 overall pick of this year’s draft, Delane has recorded five passes defensed, three tackles for loss, and an interception in five games. We’ll see if Delane is able to participate in Kansas City’s first practice of the week on Wednesday.

item.title: TNF dips to 16.56 million for Panthers-Packers
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Thursday Night Football continues to draw larger audiences, generally.
item.content:encoded:
Thursday Night Football continues to draw larger audiences, generally. Specifically, there will be some peaks and valleys.

In Week 7, Patriots-Bears racked up 19.86 million for Prime Video. In Week 8, the number for Panthers-Packers fell to 16.56 million.

While it was a 26-percent bump over the Chargers' 37-10 blowout of the Vikings in Week 8 of the 2025 season (13.13 million), it also landed a full one million below the season-to-date average of 17.56 million for TNF.

This week, a Jaguars-Ravens game that looked very good on paper as of Sunday morning has become a much more questionable endeavor, given the injuries to Baltimore quarterbacks Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley. It could be undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano under center for the Ravens.

Which won't be good for business. But will be good for the Jaguars.

item.title: Jason Witten reportedly becomes the offensive play-caller at Oklahoma
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: If, as some believe, former Cowboys tight end Jason Witten is destined to eventually become the head coach of America's team, he's taking the next step in his coaching career with Oklahoma's team.
item.content:encoded:
If, as some believe, former Cowboys tight end Jason Witten is destined to eventually become the head coach of America's team, he's taking the next step in his coaching career with Oklahoma's team.

Via SoonerScoop.com, Witten will become the offensive play-caller at the University of Oklahoma, following the in-season firing of offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle.

Witten has been serving as the Sooners' tight ends coach. He had been a high-school coach since 2021.

The 44-year-old Witten initially retired after 15 seasons with the Cowboys, worked on Monday Night Football for a season, and then returned to the NFL for 2019 (with the Cowboys) and 2020 (with the Raiders). He's in his first year as a college coach.

Whether he eventually works for the Cowboys as an assistant coach or is eventually hired to run the whole show, there's a sense that Witten will inevitably be on the Dallas staff.

item.title: Mike Vrabel on A.J. Brown: We'll see how he progresses during the week
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Patriots receiver A.J.
item.content:encoded:
Patriots receiver A.J. Brown was not able to play in the Week 8 win over the Dolphins due to a knee injury.

At this point, it's unclear if Brown will be on the field for Week 9.

“We’ll see how he progresses during the week. He’s getting treatment here,” Vrabel said Monday, via Karen Guregian of MassLive.com. “We’ll see Wednesday what those guys that were unavailable for the game, and what they look like and whatever came up during the game.”

Brown, in his first season with the Patriots, has played just three games so far this year. He’s caught just nine passes for 101 yards in those contests.

The wideout previously missed time with a high-ankle sprain.

Vrabel was similarly mum about the status of tight end Hunter Henry, who is dealing with a foot injury.

But Vrabel said Mack Hollins and Reggie Gilliam could “potentially” get back on the practice field, with both players currently on injured reserve.

The Patriots will host the Packers on Sunday afternoon in Week 9.

item.title: Hammond isn't giving up on Bears making a move to Indiana
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Bears are where we thought they were.
item.content:encoded:
The Bears are where we thought they were. And it appears they’ll be staying.

But Indiana isn't giving up just yet. Hammond Mayor Thomas McDermott Jr. believes the Bears will still cross the border.

At times, however, he wonders what will happen.

“There’s some days when you talk to me and ask, ‘Mayor, are the Bears coming,’ and I’ll be 100% positive and there’s some days that I’m not as positive, OK?" McDermott said Friday, via Doug Ross of the Post-Tribune. "And that’s because it’s changing every second.”

The one constant throughout the change is the perception that Hammond is simply a bluff for the Bears to get a deal done in Illinois.

“I think the Bears are dead serious, but what if they are playing us?" McDermott said. "What are you supposed to do?”

Hammond remains in a nothing-to-lose posture. It's not as if they're talking to two NFL teams and could potentially miss out on one by focusing on the other. It's the Bears or nothing.

Obviously, there's an investment of time and money that Hammond has made for something that could be a waste of both. What should Hammond do? Frankly, it should issue an ultimatum to the Bears.

Get it done or get lost. Break ground or get bent.

Hammond has allowed itself to become the leverage for the Bears to build a new stadium in Illinois. To those on the outside, it's obvious. To those calling the shots in Hammond, they've become sufficiently smitten by the possibility of getting the Bears that they have suspended disbelief.

To the obvious benefit of the Bears.

In the end, what will Hammond get? A fruit basket? A heartfelt "thank you"?

Either way, Hammond won't be getting an NFL team in an NFL stadium. Unless and until all options in Illinois evaporate and the Bears sign the paperwork and at least 24 NFL teams authorize the relocation and the shovels are buried in Hammond soil.

For now, Hammond should use those shovels in an effort to clear away any and all BS and force the Bears to commit.

item.title: Saints still deciding if Jordyn Tyson, Travis Etienne will return to practice this week
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Saints have yet to see rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson in game action, but they would move closer to that moment if the first-round pick is designated for return from injured reserve this week.
item.content:encoded:
The Saints have yet to see rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson in game action, but they would move closer to that moment if the first-round pick is designated for return from injured reserve this week.

Tyson has been out since injuring his hamstring this summer and head coach Kellen Moore told reporters on Monday that the team is still working through a decision on opening the wideout's return window. If he does practice Wednesday, Tyson will have 21 days to work with the team before he must be activated and he can be activated at any point in that window.

Moore said the case is similar for running back Travis Etienne and left tackle Kelvin Banks. Etienne has been out since Week 3 with a hamstring injury and Banks sprained his ankle in Week 2.

Getting all three back would be a positive development for the Saints offense as the team tries to improve on a 2-5 start to the season.

item.title: Mike Vrabel on Andy Borregales: Have confidence in him, but he's got to make his kicks
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Patriots kicker Andy Borregales missed a 40-yard field goal on Sunday against the Dolphins, but head coach Mike Vrabel hasn't lost confidence in him.
item.content:encoded:
Patriots kicker Andy Borregales missed a 40-yard field goal on Sunday against the Dolphins, but head coach Mike Vrabel hasn't lost confidence in him. At least not yet.

Borregales has now missed three field goals (from 40, 38 and 47 yards) and one extra point this season, and the longest kick he has made is 50 yards. That's not great, and Vrabel acknowledged that the Patriots need Borregales to make his kicks.

When a reporter said to Vrabel at his Monday morning press conference that it seems like Borregales has missed a lot of kicks, Vrabel said, “It doesn't seem like he has, he has, and that needs to get corrected."

But Vrabel then added that he remains confident in his kicker.

"Got a lot of confidence in Andy," Vrabel said. "I think when you see the timing and when the approach is in rhythm, it looks really good. We have to make our kicks. Everybody has a job here. There's no real message, it's, Hey, we gotta make 'em. But I've got a lot of confidence. I thought he did a really good job on the kickoff. And hopefully he's making a lot of extra points and not having him kick a lot of field goals."

It doesn't sound like Borregales is getting cut any time soon, but that could change if he has another miss this week.

item.title: Saquon Barkley's commitment to the Eagles is impressive
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Eagles won't be trading running back Saquon Barkley.
item.content:encoded:
The Eagles won't be trading running back Saquon Barkley. For most players on teams that are falling apart, the inability to chase a championship with a high-end contender would be viewed as bad news. Barkley’s comments after Philly's latest loss make it clear that he welcomes the opportunity to stick around.

It's impressive that Barkley is committed to a seemingly lost cause. Of course, the decision not to trade Barkley doesn't mean the team is committed to Barkley for as long as he wants to play in Philadelphia.

Trading him would spark a $26 million dead-money charge in 2027. It's possible that the Eagles listened, talked, and decided that the offers from any interested teams weren't good enough to justify losing the player and taking the cap hit.

Regardless, the Eagles currently are fading fast. After starting 2-0, they've lost six in a row — with four of the losses playing out in standalone windows. The 2025 Super Bowl season has disappeared into the deepest recesses of the rear-view mirror. The roster has a growing list of flaws, and the future of quarterback Jalen Hurts hovers over everything.

For now, Barkley's future is settled. He'll stick around. And he wants to.

"I have nothing but respect for this organization, top to bottom. I really do think they do things the right way," Barkley said Sunday night, via Tim McManus of ESPN. "It's an honor and a privilege every single time I get to go out there and play for this organization and put on the midnight green."

It's a great attitude from the player. The inescapable reality, from the team's perspective, is that Barkley will be wearing midnight green only until the clock strikes midnight on the team's decision to advance its "best interests" by moving on.

item.title: Jim Harbaugh: "We're aware of what the issues are, and we're the only ones who can fix them"
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: It's gotten ugly for the Chargers, who fell to 0-7 with Sunday's loss to the cross-town Rams.
item.content:encoded:
It's gotten ugly for the Chargers, who fell to 0-7 with Sunday's loss to the cross-town Rams.

Despite coming off their bye, the Chargers could not get much going offensively under beleaguered coordinator Mike McDaniel. Justin Herbert threw two more interceptions, giving him a league-high 10 through seven games. He was also strip-sacked, which was nearly picked up for a scoop-and-score.

Having kicked three field goals on Sunday, the Chargers haven’t scored a touchdown since late in the third quarter of their Week 5 loss to the Broncos.

“Yeah, aware of that and keep working, keep studying,” head coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters in his postgame press conference. “It's not a familiar position for any of the guys in our locker room, so we're the only ones who can change it. We are highly motivated and dedicated to do that.”

Asked if he’s worried about Herbert’s turnovers, Harbaugh said, “Yeah, we're aware of what the issues are, and we're the only ones who can fix them.”

McDaniel will continue to call plays, Harbaugh said. Though pressed on why he’s confident this group can turn it around, Harbaugh did not provide much of a concrete answer.

“First of all, it's a team effort, and we're going to look at the film,” Harbaugh said. “We're going to address our issues, where we can get better, and just keep working. That's highly motivated and dedicated to getting this right.

“We're the only ones that have the opportunity to change it, to fix it. And that's what we're going to do, go back to work. I have not been in this position that many times either, here as a coach. But I know we have to be dedicated ourselves to getting this turned. That's where we're at.”

The Chargers will be at home to play the Texans in Week 9.

item.title: Kirk Cousins: Brock Bowers is like Justin Jefferson, when he's covered, you still need to throw it
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins has played with his share of big-time pass catchers throughout his 15-year career.
item.content:encoded:
Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins has played with his share of big-time pass catchers throughout his 15-year career.

He’s now connecting with Brock Bowers on a weekly basis, with Bowers catching seven passes for 92 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday’s 38-33 victory over the Jets.

But even though Bowers is technically a tight end, Cousins related throwing to him to passing to an elite wide receiver.

“I think what’s hard is when you play with Pierre Garçon, DeSean Jackson, or Justin Jefferson, you’re used to throwing to guys who are really open,” Cousins said in his postgame press conference. "There were times, even when they would get doubled and I would progress off of them, and [Vikings head coach] Kevin O’Connell would say to me, ‘Still throw it to Justin when he’s covered.’ I was like, ‘I don’t like throwing to covered guys. I like throwing to open guys.’

“The coaching point with Brock has been like it was with Justin, where it’s like, when he’s covered, you still need to throw it. That kind of breaks my instincts. My instincts are to progress and throw to open guys. I think you can see there are moments this year where I can be better, and then there are moments where I’m starting to figure that out. He’s made me right, if you will.”

That coaching point sure seemed relevant for Cousins’ first touchdown of the game, when Bowers was covered and interfered with, but still managed to catch the ball for a 12-yard score.

Through six games this season, Bowers has 41 receptions for 547 yards with five touchdowns.

item.title: Von Miller defends Cowboys' coaching staff
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Cowboys linebacker Von Miller got his first sack in eight games with the team during Sunday's mind-boggling home loss to the Cardinals.
item.content:encoded:
Cowboys linebacker Von Miller got his first sack in eight games with the team during Sunday's mind-boggling home loss to the Cardinals. After the 33-30 overtime defeat, Miller went to bat for the coaching staff.

“I’m a parent," Miller said, via Jon Machota of The Athletic. "I got three kids. Sometimes you raise your kids a certain way and you teach them lessons. You expect them to act a certain way when they go out.

“And sometimes the kids just go out there and do things that are not a reflection of who you are as a parent. And I use that reference for our coaching staff. We have amazing coaches that keep us prepared, ready to go mentally, physically, emotionally. They breathe life into us, and just for whatever reason, that’s the product.

“The product that went out there is not a reflection of our coaching staff. This is pro sports. This is not parenting. So at the end of the day, the buck has to stop somewhere. Somebody’s going to get the blame.

“But my opinion, this is just me, I don’t know nothing about football. I only played 16 years. We’ve got great coaches. We’ve got a great coaching staff. And that’s not a reflection of how they coach us and get us ready every week.”

Miller's metaphor has obvious limits. For starters, it's a lot harder to disown a child than it is to bench or cut a player. If players aren't doing what they're supposed to be doing, the team needs better players.

Or it needs a better General Manager. Which won't happen, because Jerry Jones continues to do the job he hired himself to do in 1989.

As it relates to coaching, the fact that the players aren't performing the way they're supposed to shows that the coaching isn't working. If a coach tells the players "this is what you should do" and they don't do it, it's absolutely a reflection of the coach's inability to get the players to respond to the coaching.

For any great coach in any sport, the quality of the strategies hinges on the willingness and the ability of the players to do what they are told to do. The coach's job includes not only drawing up the plays but getting the players to implement them as designed.

It's that simple. And, no, it's not parenting. Parents love their children unconditionally. A coach's love is conditioned on the player doing what the player is expected to do. When the player can't (for whatever reason) or won't, the coach needs to pivot to a different player.

So if the Cowboys' 3-5 record doesn't land on the shoulders of the coaching staff, where should it go? And if it goes to the overall quality of the roster, isn't the general "indictment of the whole show" (as Jones said Sunday) a specific indictment of it ringleader?

If the Cowboys have the right coaches and the wrong players, it means they have the wrong G.M. And since the owner is the G.M., the cycle will continue.

Offseason hype, in-season collapse. Lather, rinse, repeat.

And as long as the fans keep falling for it, it will continue — year after year after year. The common denominator since the team's most recent NFC Championship appearance is the G.M. who, if he wasn't the owner, would have been fired four or five times since 1995.

item.title: Aaron Glenn says Jets aren't trading Breece Hall
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Breece Hall missed his fifth straight game with a quad injury on Sunday and Braelon Allen continued to shine in his absence.
item.content:encoded:
Breece Hall missed his fifth straight game with a quad injury on Sunday and Braelon Allen continued to shine in his absence.

Allen ran 21 times for 147 yards and a touchdown in the 38-33 loss to the Raiders and he's averaging just over 100 yards a game while Hall has been out of the lineup. Hall has practiced the last two weeks and he's been scratched after being listed as questionable, which has joined Allen's performance as reasons for some to wonder if the Jets might be thinking about trading Hall ahead of the November 10 deadline.

At a Monday morning press conference, head coach Aaron Glenn said that will not happen.

"Breece is still a part of this team," Glenn said, via Zack Rosenblatt of TheAthletic.com. "I've said it before: We're in the business of keeping good players and he's one of our better players so he'll be here."

The Jets have also reportedly rebuffed overtures from teams interested in trading for wide receiver Garrett Wilson, so it does not appear that their 2-6 start is going to lead to a fire sale over the next week.

item.title: Garrett Wilson: We have to give our fans a reason to come out
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: If someone flipped on Sunday's game between the Raiders and the Jets in the fourth quarter, they would have been forgiven for wondering if the Raiders were the home team at MetLife Stadium.
item.content:encoded:
If someone flipped on Sunday's game between the Raiders and the Jets in the fourth quarter, they would have been forgiven for wondering if the Raiders were the home team at MetLife Stadium.

Raiders fans were loud enough in big moments of the game to contribute to a Jets false start and the interception by Raiders safety Jeremy Chinn to seal the 38-33 win was greeted with lusty cheers by those same fans. The loss dropped the Jets to 2-6 on the season and wide receiver Garrett Wilson said after the game that it is up to the Jets to do more to convince their own fans to make that kind of an impact.

“They had some fans in the building," Wilson said, via SNY. "We gotta handle it. . . . We got to give our fans a reason to come out. I get it. As a team we got to operate better, regardless of the noise.”

The Jets are on their way to a 16th straight season without a trip to the playoffs and that run of futility makes it more surprising that they still have enough supporters turning out on Sundays to make it a surprise when the visiting side dominates the stands.

item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Buccaneers shut out the Falcons in Sunday's win, but their defense lost a starter to injury on the way to victory.
item.content:encoded:
The Buccaneers shut out the Falcons in Sunday's win, but their defense lost a starter to injury on the way to victory.

Linebacker Yaya Diaby left the game with a knee injury. Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that Diaby is believed to have a sprained MCL and he is set to have an MRI to provide further clarity on the extent of the injury. That testing will also provide a better idea of when Diaby is able to return to the lineup.

Diaby was limited to seven snaps against Atlanta.

Diaby did not land on the stat sheet during his brief time in Sunday's game, but he has 16 tackles, three sacks and an interception over the course of the entire season.

item.title: Joe Burrow: We found a way to win, we didn't do that the last few years
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Bengals apparently need to dig themselves a 13-0 hole before they're ready to start playing football this season.
item.content:encoded:
The Bengals apparently need to dig themselves a 13-0 hole before they're ready to start playing football this season.

The Bengals spotted the Ravens that lead in the first half of Week 7 before rallying for a 35-13 win and they found themselves down 13-0 in the first quarter against the Titans this Sunday. They didn't wait until the second half to get their act together this week, but they had to struggle the whole way before finally nailing down a 43-36 overtime win.

Burrow and others fielded questions about their slow starts in their postgame press conferences, but Burrow was more interested in the final scores because he feels that scrapping out wins like their last two are a sign that the team has fixed part of what has ailed them the last few years.

"We found a way to win today. We're 5-2," Burrow said, via a transcript from the team. "We lose that game for the last three years. It's hard to win. You want to be great snap in snap out, but it's not the reality of it. All we can do is keep working hard and get better. You win from wins and losses and good plays and bad plays. That's what the NFL and getting better is. We'll continue to do that."

Burrow threw three interceptions to go with five touchdown passes and his game-winning touchdown run on Sunday. He acknowledged the need to "be better and limit those critical mistakes," but returned often to the theme of finding ways to win when they would have fallen apart in the past.

item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Tyler Huntley has replcaed Jackson.
item.content:encoded:
The Ravens have ruled out Lamar Jackson. The question is: How bad is his right thumb injury?

Jackson started for the first time since Oct. 4, missing the past three games with a high ankle sprain, but he lasted one play against the Bills.

The Ravens quarterback got hit on an incompletion intended for Zay Flowers and immediately left the field. The team’s medical staff took him to the X-ray room.

Tyler Huntley, who was 1-2 in Jackson's absence, replaced him. He is 2-for-3 for no yards.

The Bills lead 10-7 after a Josh Allen pass intended for tight end Jackson Hawes was batted into the air by Hawes and defensive lineman Broderick Washington intercepted it at the Buffalo 17. The Ravens scored on Derrick Henry's 2-yard run.

Henry is only the third player in NFL history to record 40 or more rushing touchdowns with two different franchises.

item.title: Jaylen Warren rushes for 143 on his birthday, Steelers beat Browns 27-6
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The streak continues for the Steelers and Browns in Pittsburgh.
item.content:encoded:
The streak continues for the Steelers and Browns in Pittsburgh.

With both teams entering the contest at 5-2, Pittsburgh ran all over Cleveland to come away with a dominant 27-6 victory.

The Steelers took control of the game in the first half and never really let it go, using a punishing running attack. The club had 160 yards on the ground in the first half, finishing with 201 yards in the category for the game.

On his 28th birthday, Jaylen Warren led the way with 143 yards on 17 carries with a touchdown — including a 51-yard scamper. Rico Dowdle was plenty effective, too, rushing for 56 yards on 15 carries.

Pat Freiermuth got into the ground game with a 1-yard tush push touchdown at the end of the first half.

Aaron Rodgers wasn’t asked to do too much and did not need to, ending the game 13-of-25 for 172 yards with an interception. The pick went right off of DK Metcalf’s hands before Denzel Ward came away with it.

Big tight end Darnell Washington led with three catches for 94 yards.

For Cleveland, Deshaun Watson passed for over 300 yards for a second consecutive game. But he was largely stymied by the Pittsburgh defense, which produced a strip-sack on him in the first quarter that led to a touchdown.

Watson finished the contest 27-of-39 for 324 yards. He was sacked eight times.

Harold Fannin led with 154 yards on 10 catches.

The Browns still have not won a regular-season game in Pittsburgh since 2003.

At 6-2, the Steelers will be on their bye in Week 9.

The 5-3 Browns will be on the road to face the Saints next Sunday.

item.title: Cowboys had never blown a 14-point, fourth-quarter lead at home before Sunday
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: A third-party contractor yelled "embarrassing" to Dak Prescott as he walked back to the Cowboys' locker room after a 24-16 loss to the Bucs in Week 5.
item.content:encoded:
A third-party contractor yelled "embarrassing" to Dak Prescott as he walked back to the Cowboys' locker room after a 24-16 loss to the Bucs in Week 5. The Cowboys' 33-30 overtime loss to the Cardinals on Sunday was arguably worse.

Before Sunday, the Cowboys were 202-0-1 when leading by 14 or more points in the fourth quarter at home in their history, including the postseason, according to ESPN.

On Sunday, the Cowboys led 24-10 with 14:20 remaining in regulation.

It matched the largest blown fourth-quarter lead in team history. In 2011 and 2022, the Cowboys blew fourth-quarter leads at the Jets and at the Packers, respectively. They are now 342-3-1 in franchise history when leading by at least 14 points in the fourth quarter.

Owner Jerry Jones called in "an indictment of the whole show."

"We had numerable chances to win this game and didn't do it," Jones said. "And I know everybody . . . is disappointed. We came out the second half and were a shadow of ourselves. So there's nothing to point to other than we just weren't a good team in the second half."

The Cowboys became the first team in the NFL this season to lose when leading by at least 14 points in the fourth. Teams were 44-0-1 in that situation entering Sunday.

item.title: The Vikings should explore a trade for Daniel Jones
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Kevin O'Connell's decision to punt with 3:01 to play speaks volumes about the level of trust in Kyler Murray.
item.content:encoded:
At a time when the Vikings are believed to be talking to the Colts about a potential trade for running back Jonathan Taylor, they should adjust their focal point, just a bit.

The Vikings should be talking to the Colts about a potential trade for quarterback Daniel Jones.

When the thought first popped into my somewhat relaxed brain on Sunday, I was mostly kidding. After reflecting on Sunday's 19-15 loss to the Lions — and revisiting the rare displays of frustration from receiver Justin Jefferson late in the game and, even more significantly, from coach Kevin O'Connell when talking to quarterback Kyler Murray after an ugly interception late in the first half — it's not a joke.

They should immediately pivot from Taylor to Jones.

The Vikings had Jones in the building two years ago, after he was released by the Giants. They wanted to keep him for 2025, more (by all appearances) than they wanted to keep Sam Darnold. (Indeed, there were whispers of a potential benching of Darnold for Jones in the 2024 postseason.)

Now that the Colts are in full-blown pre-rebuild mode, trading Jones should be part of the effort to clear the decks (and stockpile picks) for the next G.M. And while the Colts have a window to avoid more than $10 million of Jones's $38 million compensation package for 2027 via a trade in the early days of the new league year in March, they could get more now from a contender that envisions Jones as an immediate upgrade.

Jones obviously won't be the long-term answer in Indianapolis. And he would undoubtedly welcome the chance to move on from a team that prematurely threw in the towel last week by trading guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner.

In Minnesota, Jones would be an immediate upgrade over Kyler Murray. The difference between Jones vs. Murray could be more significant than the difference between Jonathan Taylor and Aaron Jones/Jordan Mason. Which, if accurate, would result in a bigger overall bump to the offense.

The Vikings have a championship-caliber defense, thanks in large part to the work of defensive coordinator Brian Flores. The grind-it-out-and-get-a-win formula had been working — until it didn't.

Here's the inescapable reality. When they win with quarterback play that is inconsistent and, in turn, frustrating to people like Jefferson and O'Connell, it's easy to overlook the flaws and keep pushing forward. When they lose, the frustrations of that moment become compounded by the lingering frustrations regarding plays and points left on the field in the wins that were salvaged by the defense.

Whether it's Jones or someone else (including a possible pivot to Carson Wentz), O'Connell and G.M. Nolan Teasley need to conduct a frank, candid, and objective assessment of the quarterback play under Murray. The fact that they picked Murray over J.J. McCarthy shouldn't be a factor. That's the kind of pride/ego consideration that keeps dysfunctional teams dysfunctional by doubling down on a mistake instead of admitting it and moving on.

The Vikings need to realize that: (1) the defense is great; (2) the running game is good enough; and (3) the passing game is too spotty to be expected to make a big play in a big spot.

Consider the decision that O'Connell made with 3:01 to play on Sunday, when the Vikings faced fourth and five from their own 33. Down four points after the Detroit running game had hot-knife-through-buttered their way to the go-ahead touchdown, why give the ball back to the Lions and let them close out the game by continuing to lean on Jahmyr Gibbs?

In that moment, O'Connell thought the chances of winning were enhanced by punting — not by asking the offense to gain five yards in a gotta-have-it situation.

While the choice showed unwarranted confidence in the defense, it showed NO confidence in the quarterback.

Frankly, that one specific decision from O'Connell leads naturally to the next, more consequential decision that the organization must make. If O'Connell doesn't trust the offense under Murray to gain five yards with the game on the line, the Vikings should no longer entrust the offense to Murray.

It's that simple. And, if the Vikings hope to avoid an outcome to the season that will result in an every-other-year playoff appearance and another one-and-done postseason, they'll make the decision that someone other than Murray should be playing quarterback.

At a time when politics have become a major national focal point, this would be a so-called 80-20 issue among Vikings fans. They've seen the "just good enough is just good enough" movie for decades. With the defense the Vikings currently have, the offense needs more. If they're serious about having a snowball's chance in San Diego to get back to the Super Bowl for the first time in 50 years, they'll send Kyler to Belize and make a play for Jones.

Or someone else. See if the Raiders are willing to part with Kirk Cousins (they shouldn't be, but why not make the call?) Call the Chargers about Justin Herbert. Scour every depth chart and start doing the due diligence.

When Cousins suffered a season-ending torn Achilles tendon just before the trade deadline in 2023, the Vikings mobilized instantly to find a replacement. Based on the full body of work from Murray to date in 2026, they should be doing the same thing now — if they want to parlay their 6-0 start into the best possible finish.

item.title: Joe Brady: Sunday's performance is the expectation for our defense
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Bills allowed an average of 28.5 points per game in their first six games of the 2026 season and improving on that was a focus for the team during their bye week.
item.content:encoded:
The Bills allowed an average of 28.5 points per game in their first six games of the 2026 season and improving on that was a focus for the team during their bye week.

Sunday's return to action resulted in much better numbers. They allowed the Ravens 144 yards in a 36-10 win that moved their record to 6-1 on the season. After the game was over, head coach Joe Brady said he wants the unit to look at that performance as their standard for the rest of the season.

"I think our defense should look at today and understand that that’s what the expectation is," Brady said, via the team's website. "And I'm not talking about the production. I'm not talking about the takeaways and sacks. I'm talking about the style that they played, the way that they flew around. Look, I'm just watching it out there, but I think the silent tape's going to speak loudly in terms of the way that they played for one another, the way they ran around, the communication. Everything we challenged them with coming off the bye, I thought they responded to it, and they just kept going."

Brady's message was about the defense, but it's hard to ignore what was going on for the Ravens offense. Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley both left the game with injuries, which meant undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano was pressed into action for the first time in the NFL.

Fagnano was overmatched, but future Bills opponents won't be quite so hamstrung and the Buffalo defense will have to show that they are able to match that level of play against all comers.

item.title: Justin Herbert has gone eight straight starts without multiple TDs
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: As the 0-6 Chargers emerge from their bye with a "visit" to the Rams, quarterback Justin Herbert will be trying to reverse a horrible trend.
item.content:encoded:
As the 0-6 Chargers emerge from their bye with a "visit" to the Rams, quarterback Justin Herbert will be trying to reverse a horrible trend.

Herbert has gone eight straight games, including the postseason, without multiple total touchdowns. Via NBC Sports research, only one quarterback in Chargers history has gone at least nine straight starts without multiple touchdowns.

The record is held by former first-rounder Ryan Leaf, who went 12 straight starts without multiple touchdowns from 1998 through 2000.

Herbert also leads the league with 10 turnovers. The Chargers nevertheless are sticking with offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, at least for now.

An embarrassment against the team with which they share a stadium could change things, quickly.

item.title: Baker Mayfield on zero completed passes: Whatever it takes to win
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Buccaneers set a franchise-record with 324 rushing yards in Sunday's 16-0 win over the Falcons and they made a little other history as well.
item.content:encoded:
The Buccaneers set a franchise-record with 324 rushing yards in Sunday's 16-0 win over the Falcons and they made a little other history as well.

The Bucs did not have a completed pass in the game, which was a first in franchise history and it made them the first team since the Bills in 1974 to go an entire game without completing a pass. The game was played in wet and sloppy conditions that joined Bucs quarterback Baker Mayfield's injured right thumb as reasons why the Bucs only tried three passes all game.

“I’ll do whatever it takes to win,” Mayfield said, via Rob Maaddi of the Associated Press. “That’s all that matters to me.”

Mayfield was 7-of-11 in Tampa's Week 7 win over the Panthers and the team has called a total of 16 pass plays over the last two weeks. They've called 104 running plays and the back-to-back wins should serve as proof of concept for a run-focused approach no matter the weather in the weeks to come.

item.title: Dak Prescott: "Cowardice" to put blame for Sunday's loss on Brian Schottenheimer
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Cowboys blew a 14-point lead and lost at home for the first time in franchise history on Sunday, so quarterback Dak Prescott may have been understating things when he called it "one of the toughest" losses of his career.
item.content:encoded:
The Cowboys blew a 14-point lead and lost at home for the first time in franchise history on Sunday, so quarterback Dak Prescott may have been understating things when he called it "one of the toughest" losses of his career.

Arizona scored 20 points in the final 11 minutes of regulation and then missed an extra point that would have given them a win. That reprieve did not spark the Cowboys as they went three-and-out on their only possession before the Cardinals' game-winning field goal in overtime.

The magnitude of the collapse during a season that has featured other underwhelming performances has led to questions about head coach Brian Schottenheimer's job security. Prescott was adamant after the loss that all can't be put on Schottenheimer's shoulders.

"It's all of us," Prescott said, via the team's website. "Don't put the blame on one person. Simple as that. I think that's weak. I think that's cowardice. This game is about all 11 that touch the field and every person that has a part in it coaches and support staff. It's never just one person's fault. Even if I go out there and throw a bunch of interceptions, it's never just truly one person's fault. And so, don't take the easy and cheap way out. This is about us and it's about us backing him up and backing one another up and we'll have to show it."

Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said he’s not thinking about an in-season coaching change, but he also called the loss an "indictment of the whole show" and Schottenheimer's job puts him at the top of the pyramid. That could wind up working out well for him if the 3-5 team can navigate its way past the Giants to win the NFC East, but there's been little about their performance to this point in the season to suggest they're capable of that kind of consistent success.

item.title: Frustrated Justin Jefferson didn't speak to reporters after Sunday's loss
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: When a team is winning, it's hard for any offensive players who aren't getting the ball as often as they should to be upset.
item.content:encoded:
When a team is winning, it's hard for any offensive players who aren't getting the ball as often as they should to be upset. When winning becomes losing, the frustrations can quickly surface.

That happened for the Vikings on Sunday against the Lions. Receiver Justin Jefferson, who made a spectacular touchdown catch in the first half, didn't see the ball as often as he should have during proverbial nut-cutting time.

After the Vikings' final drive — which curiously ended on a fourth-and-five punt with 3:01 to play at a time when the Detroit rushing game was clicking — Jefferson made a rare display of frustration. After the 19-15 loss, Jefferson declined to speak to reporters, per Kevin Seifert of ESPN.

Which means that Jefferson, who has a habit of always saying all the right things, doubted that he would have been able to do that.

"Obviously he's frustrated, and that's understandable," quarterback Kyler Murray told reporters, via Seifert. "He is who he is, and he has every right to the way he feels when he doesn't get the ball. That's on us to find a way to get him the ball."

"We had some opportunities for [Jefferson], and there were some chances there," coach Kevin O'Connell told reporters. "But we've got to find a way to get him the ball, especially on potential chances for him on some of those sequences where we're looking to kick off some momentum. He's a great guy to do it behind, and we'll continue to find ways to get him the football. But it was a division game. These guys want to win. I don't fault the frustration or the competitiveness in any way, shape or form."

Whatever the cause, there's clearly a problem. And Murray, who missed time early in the season due to a concussion, should be up to speed now. On Sunday, he wasn't good enough.

And here's the basic reality. At some point, either en route to the playoffs or after the Vikings get there, Murray will have to make a big play in a big spot. The jury is out on whether he will.

The Vikings don't have many options. They could try to make a trade, but who's out there? They wanted to keep Daniel Jones after the 2024 season; maybe, at this point, the Colts would welcome the chance to move on.

If the Raiders had lost to the Jets, Kirk Cousins may have been available for a reunion. With Las Vegas now at 4-4, why would they move him?

The other option would be to ride with Carson Wentz, who has shown that he can and will get the ball to Jefferson.

However it goes, Sunday's game exposed the biggest problem with the Vikings. Against teams that can't be held to 15 points or less, the Vikings may not be able to muster enough points to beat them.

item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Jaguars defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton was carted off on Sunday, and the initial prognosis isn't good.
item.content:encoded:
Jaguars defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton was carted off on Sunday, and the initial prognosis isn't good.

The Jaguars believe Hamilton has a torn quad and will have to miss the rest of the season, according to Ian Rapoport. Hamilton will have more tests today to confirm the diagnosis.

The 6-foot-4, 335-pound Hamilton has started every game and played well for the Jaguars this season. He even filled in at long snapper for a game and performed respectably. He'll be a tough player to replace.

A 2020 third-round pick, Hamilton has played his entire career in Jacksonville but is slated to become a free agent after this season.

item.title: Lions say Jack Campbell will remain hospitalized overnight
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Lions linebacker Jack Campbell will be hospitalized overnight after suffering what appeared to be a serious injury on Sunday against the Vikings.
item.content:encoded:
Lions linebacker Jack Campbell will be hospitalized overnight after suffering what appeared to be a serious injury on Sunday against the Vikings.

The Lions released a statement three hours after today's game in Detroit ended to say that Campbell is being evaluated.

"Jack Campbell is resting and will remain in a local hospital tonight, for continued evaluation and monitoring. The team will provide further updates as we have them," the statement said.

Campbell was motionless on the field for several minutes after a collision, and players on both teams were visibly shaken by the injury. The Lions have said Campbell is alert and breathing but have not offered any clarification about whether Campbell has movement in his extremities.
